mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in the unemployment rate above 4.0% signals weakening labor market conditions, reducing corporate earnings growth and pushing the S&P 500 lower over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative in periods where UNRATE exceeds 4.0% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals deteriorating household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS declines > 2% over two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month acceleration in the industrial production index (INDPRO) above 0.5% signals improved manufacturing activity, which boosts earnings and drives the S&P 500 higher over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when INDPRO rises > 0.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, which drives the S&P 500 lower over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
